messages.author: 065110cca96a6373
messages.subject: flag that knitr is running?
parts:
Hi All,

Are there any reliable flags that a function could use to tell if it is being run by knitr rather than a plain R script/interactively?  I am not looking for interactive/non interactive, but something knitr specific.

One approach is to look up something knitr would have, like an option that was set:

# add this to when knitr is run
opts_knit$set(knitrON=TRUE)

# have function check for this (exists() incase knitr is not loaded)
exists("opts_knit") && opts_knit$get("knitrON")

Is there a cleaner/safer way?

Thanks!

Josh


--

messages.subject: Re: [knitr] flag that knitr is running?

messages.author: cc1ef8c8158d6b73
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] flag that knitr is running?
parts:
Exactly. I'm also wonder why you need such a flag. There is indeed a
flag, getOption('knitr.in.progress') (TRUE if knitting is in progress,
NULL otherwise), but I do not consider it "reliable", since anyone can
set options(knitr.in.progress = TRUE) anywhere.

If you want to change the printing behavior of knitr, you may want to
take a look at the knit_print methods in this example:
http://yihui.name/printr/

Regards,
Yihui
--
Yihui Xie <xiey...@gmail.com>
Web: http://yihui.name

messages.author: 065110cca96a6373
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] flag that knitr is running?
parts:
Yihui,

Thanks for the information!

It is a bit obscure behavior, but the use case is specific.  Basically, if the code is being knit into a report, it should just report the key information, if it is run separately, it prints more verbose output (a bit like an automatic verbose flag).

Certainly I could add a couple lines of code so that everything runs, but only the bit I want is actually printed in the report, but that is a bit of extra code everytime versus a simple hack: verbose = isTRUE(getOption('knit.in.progress')).

It only needs to be "reliable" in the sense that I can specify whatever knitr options I want without fear that my check gets broken in this specific case.

Anyway, much appreciate the help!

Josh

messages.author: 8502567f9dbc7c7e
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] flag that knitr is running?
parts: It is that very use-case specificity that makes it obscure. It is so much more clear to whoever is reading it later why the output is different if you explicitly specify the verbose flag as needed. Just make your default verbosity match your non-knitr use case, and specify the verbosity when you are in a knitted document.

messages.subject: Re: [knitr] flag that knitr is running?
parts:
Sounds like a nice tweak.

Right now I'm investing time in developing a personal philosophy for
handling such a need.

My tentative approach is to first "compile" the entirety of the
document, computed data, and images, and then use those artifacts to
produce other 'subsetted' documents that don't require it all.

That is the plan, no result to report yet, but I am curious if anyone
else is pondering such things?
